title: Mestisa ampalaya (Mestisa F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Mestisa ampalaya is an F1 hybrid ampalaya variety from East West Seed. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Mestisa ampalaya is an F1 hybrid ampalaya variety, also sold or known as Mestisa F1 or Mestiza F1. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from East West Seed.

heroImage.alt: Ampalaya seedlings planted through plastic mulch on raised beds, the kind of farm where Mestisa ampalaya is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Mestisa F1 or Mestiza F1, this is the same ampalaya. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [ampalaya variety finder](/crop-varieties/ampalaya), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit ampalaya fields most often: [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [melon fly](/pests/melon-fly), [squash beetle](/pests/squash-beetle), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 42 to 45 days after planting, then about two months of picking (Agriculture Monthly).
**Fruit:** Light green, 30 to 35 cm long and 5 to 6 cm across, mostly first class (light green fruits are thought less bitter by many buyers).
High yielding, used as the scion on patola rootstock for grafted seedlings.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the hybrid of big growers in Floridablanca, Pampanga, the ampalaya capital of Central Luzon, the scion of choice for grafted ampalaya in Alcala, Pangasinan, and named with Galaxy in East West's 2025 farmer story. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Mestisa ampalaya

Pick by fruit: long and light green for most markets, short and dark for the bitter lovers. Hybrids yield more on a trellis, and some are bred to tolerate the downy mildew of the wet season. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Mestisa F1 the same as Mestisa?
items.a: Yes. Mestisa F1 is another name for Mestisa. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Mestisa?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
